goal: Boost small business in SoMa without slowing Bay Bridge traffic

options.title: Minna Street car-free + $3 AM-peak charge at the Folsom · 6th St inlet
options.rationale: This is the only plan that doesn't add delay: total delay changes by -0.46 hours. Revenue rises by $6,475, and the plan is valued at about $16.8M per year, with car commuters down 357 and walkers up 336. The trade-offs are 84 commuters who stop commuting ("gone") and 168 fewer bike commuters. The model does not report Bay Bridge or I-80 delay separately, and the $3 charge is an assumed level.

options.title: Clementina Street car-free (single street)
options.rationale: Walkers rise by 462 and revenue by $3,577, and the plan is valued at about $14.5M per year. Delay rises by 6.17 hours and car, transit and bike commuters each fall (168, 126 and 168), so it is a small gain for local shops with a small traffic cost. The model does not break out Bay Bridge delay.

options.title: Clementina + Stevenson Streets car-free
options.rationale: This plan has the highest revenue gain of the three, $6,637 per year, and walkers rise by 567. It is valued at about $17.7M per year. It adds 23.56 hours of delay, and transit commuters fall by 168, so it is the weakest fit for the goal of not slowing traffic. Choose it only if the retail gain matters more than the delay, since the model does not isolate Bay Bridge traffic.
